one_sentence_story: In 1983 in Munich, Josef Zihl and colleagues documented Patient L.M. — whose rare bilateral stroke in visual area V5/hMT+ left color and reading crystal-clear while erasing smooth visual motion so pouring tea looked frozen like a glacier and cars jumped in strobe-light frames.
so_what_for_you: Appreciate that 'seeing' isn't one thing — your brain stitches color, shape, and motion in separate specialist workshops, and when one sense falters, cross-sensory cues like rising cup sound can step right in.
